items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Laboratory Science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience (e.g. 5 years of relevant research lab experience experience)
Minimum 3 years of experience in laboratory operations, specimen receiving, accessioning, sample handling, or a comparable laboratory support environment.
Previous experience serving as a lead, supervisor, or manager in a laboratory or operational environment – preferred

The UCLA Olympic Analytical Laboratory (OAL) is one of the world’s largest World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited sports drug-testing facility and one of the leading research institutions in the field of athletic doping. Founded in 1982 by a grant from the Los Angeles Olympic Organizing Committee, the UCLA facility was the first U.S. laboratory accredited by the International Olympic Committee.
We are seeking a Laboratory Supervisor to lead the team responsible for sample receiving and accessioning operations. Key duties include:

Supervise and provide leadership to staff responsible for specimen receipt, accessioning, labeling verification, aliquoting, storage, chain-of-custody documentation, and transfer of samples to testing areas. – Preproduction of testing
Coordinate daily workflow activities to ensure timely and accurate sample intake operations.
Oversee specimen documentation, chain-of-custody processes, sample reconciliation activities, and resolution of operational issues.
Monitor inventory levels and readiness of receiving supplies, shipping materials, storage areas, and related equipment.
Ensure compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs), quality standards, laboratory safety requirements, and documentation retention policies.
Identify workflow challenges and implement practical process improvements that enhance efficiency, accuracy, and service quality.
Support the implementation of new procedures, technologies, and systems, including training staff on updated workflows and best practices.
Foster a collaborative, accountable, and customer-focused work environment that promotes continuous improvement and operational excellence.
Knowledge of specimen documentation practices, chain-of-custody requirements, SOPs, quality assurance/quality control principles, and laboratory safety standards.
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Demonstrated ability to prioritize multiple responsibilities, exercise sound judgment, and effectively manage competing deadlines in a complex environment.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work collaboratively across teams.
